content:
#1 I'm reading https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/transitive+relation

> Transitive relations are often understood as orders.

A preorder requires both transitivity and reflexivity.

What type of order can there be with just transitivity?
subject: Can transitive relation alone be understood as order?

content:
#2 While I am not the author of that remark, I guess it’s a sensible if rather unusual way to look at things — in any case it’s just a matter of using terminology. Related discussion can be seen at math.SE:a/2210713.

But I have reworded at transitive relation a little.
subject: Can transitive relation alone be understood as order?

content:
#3 Thank you, that SE link is helpfu, although a bit surprising how sparse and informal is the topic.I'll try to find more.
Regarding your rewording - based on the referenced article, it seems to allow a strengthening - that transitivity is a required property for order, but (always?) in conjunction with another property such as reflexivity/irreflexivity.
subject: Can transitive relation alone be understood as order?

content:
#4

always?

That is really the same question as #1 and so the same answer #2 still applies.

It’s a matter of terminology, only, and it makes some sense (even if nobody before said it, that happens) to declare terminology as the original author of that entry once suggested (Toby Bartels in rev 1), even if it’s non-standard. An original thought – that happens.
subject: Can transitive relation alone be understood as order?

content:
#5 Thank you. I reread it and I get it. The snag was less the terminology and more with interpretation and potential incompatibility arising further down from additional properties.

However, I should have realized that if equivalence relation as symmetric preorder is "legit", it's all good :)
subject: Can transitive relation alone be understood as order?
